::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 11th [1892]  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS UCLA: collection 100: box 95[^1]
:::

My dear [C C](people/person_329.qmd)
You may as well see this remonstrance of one of the old fashioned goody souls [Mrs Crocker](people/person_2109.qmd) her name seems to be. She goes on afterwards about [‘Amethyst’](other_books/otherbook_663.qmd)— and I won’t send that, for it is all misunderstanding. I wrote a defence of Cherry and Maisie saying that she was in a process of growth, and I also explained the scope of Amethyst and that you are not a dangerous person, but I think we must try to keep the religious element more prominent and that [Mr Innes](people/person_744.qmd) should know that in gaining the young we may be losing the sobersided goody variety—[^2]   It is the girls become the aunts.

[no signature]

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: Cherry is the hero of Coleridge's novel *An English Squire* (1881). Her novel *Amethyst: The Story of a Beauty* (1891), was favourably reviewed by Mary Bramston in *MP* (December 1891) 706.

**Note:** Innes wanted the [*MP*](organizations/other_52.qmd) to be more modern and popular, and instituted innovations which alarmed CMY.
